children.name: Project Description
children.reason:
Evaluation of the README file:

project_purpose:
Score (avg): 2.0
[QWEN] The README identifies the project as "Smart Village App - Main-Server" and states that "This main-server is one main part of the whole Smart Village App project," directing readers to https://github.com/ikuseiGmbH/smart-village-app for more information. However, it fails to explain what the Smart Village App actually does, what the main-server specifically handles (e.g., user management, POI management, GraphQL API serving), or why the project is useful to users or the community. There is no description of features, use cases, or the problem the project solves. The purpose is essentially reduced to a name and a link to another repository, leaving the reader with very little understanding of the project's value or functionality.

setup_instructions:
Score (avg): 4.0
[QWEN] The README provides a comprehensive "Setup process" section covering: Ruby 2.6.8 installation with specific environment variables, Bundler installation, master key configuration, database configuration with a full example database.yml, database/user setup via rake commands, running the server locally, and login instructions. Specific versions are provided (Ruby 2.6.8, Rails 5.2.4, Bundler 2.3.20). However, there are minor errors: a typo "Ru the following commands" instead of "Run," and the GraphQL API section lists the same file twice (doc/poi_mutation_example.graphql appears twice). Despite these small issues, the instructions are detailed, structured, and actionable enough for a developer to set up the project.

info_project_status:
Score (avg): 1.0
[QWEN] The README contains no information whatsoever about the project's status. There is no mention of whether the project is actively under development, in maintenance mode, deprecated, or no longer maintained. While CodeClimate badges (maintainability and test coverage) are present, these indicate code quality metrics rather than project activity status. There are no release notes, a "last updated" note, or any statement about the current state of development. A potential contributor or user cannot determine whether the project is actively supported or abandoned.

info_maintainer:
Score (avg): 2.0
[QWEN] The README does not include an explicit section describing who maintains or contributes to the project. The organization "ikuseiGmbH" can be inferred from the CodeClimate badge URLs and the link to the main project (github.com/ikuseiGmbH/smart-village-app), and there is a reference to visiting the "german website" (https://smart-village.app) to "get in touch with us." However, there is no dedicated maintainers/contributors section, no list of contributors, no contact information, no contribution guidelines, and no description of the team or individuals responsible for the project. The maintenance information is only implicit through URLs rather than explicitly stated.

children.name: Project Structure
children.reason:
Project structure evaluation:

directory_organization:
Score (avg): 4.0
[QWEN] Question evaluated: "The project follows appropriate directory organization conventions for its technology stack (e.g., src/, tests/, docs/)." This is a Ruby on Rails backend, and the layout is a near-textbook Rails structure: app/ contains assets/ (config, images, javascripts, stylesheets), controllers/, helpers/, jobs/, mailers/, models/, views/, plus channels/ for ActionCable, graphql/ for the API layer, and services/ for service objects. Configuration lives in config/ (application.rb, boot.rb, environment.rb, environments/, initializers/, locales/), database artifacts in db/ (migrate/, schema.rb, seeds.rb), shared code in lib/ (tasks/, assets/), and standard root files are present (Gemfile, Gemfile.lock, Rakefile, config.ru, Dockerfile, package.json). The project uses RSpec instead of Rails' default test/ directory, which is an accepted convention evidenced by .rspec, spec/rails_helper.rb, and spec/spec_helper.rb, with tests mirrored under spec/ and documentation examples under doc/. Deployment tooling (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, docker/) is sensibly placed. Minor deviations prevent a perfect score: no conventional bin/ directory appears in the tree (unusual for a modern Rails app), stack.yml is a non-standard root file, and product-specific static content (public/mobile-app/) is embedded in public/. Overall, the organization strongly follows the stack's conventions.

naming_conventions:
Score (avg): 4.0
[QWEN] Question evaluated: "The project uses consistent naming conventions for files and directories (e.g., snake_case, camelCase)." The codebase is overwhelmingly and consistently snake_case: Ruby files (application_controller.rb, assign_waste_location_to_tour.rb, gtfs_redis_adapter.rb, send_single_push_notification_job.rb), directories (data_resources/, resource_modules/, public_transportation/, input_types/, query_types/), timestamped migrations (20210216150230_create_generic_items.rb, 20220902120506_create_waste_tours.rb), view partials with underscore prefixes (_form.html.erb, _search_form.html.erb), locale files (devise.de.yml, doorkeeper.en.yml, mailers.de.yml), spec files (static_contents_controller_spec.rb), and factories (accessibility_informations.rb, notification_pushes.rb). Tooling files follow their own standard conventions (.eslintrc.json, .rubocop.yml, .gitlab-ci.yml, docker-compose.yml). Deviations are real but localized: public/mobile-app/configs/ uses camelCase (homeAbout.json, homeCarousel.json, homeService.json); the directory mobile-app/ and page smart-village-app.html use hyphens; doc/gtfs/gtfs-stops.csv uses a hyphen while sibling files routes.csv and trips.csv do not; and there is a clear typo in spec/factories/adresses.rb (should be addresses.rb, matching app/models/.../address.rb and the create_addresses migration). A legacy docker/unicorn.rb alongside config/puma.rb also hints at inconsistent server naming history. Core code naming is excellent; the static mobile-app content introduces the main inconsistencies.

separation_of_concerns:
Score (avg): 5.0
[QWEN] Question evaluated: "The project properly separates different concerns into appropriate directories (e.g., separating source, tests, configuration)." The separation is excellent. Application code is confined to app/; all tests are isolated in spec/ with a structure that mirrors app/ (spec/controllers, spec/models, spec/graphql/mutations, spec/jobs, spec/services, spec/requests, spec/routing, spec/views), plus dedicated factories/ for test data and support/ for shared test helpers. All Rails configuration is centralized in config/, with per-environment files (development.rb, production.rb, test.rb), feature-based initializers (devise.rb, doorkeeper.rb, cors.rb, rollbar.rb, delayed_job_config.rb), and locales split by feature and language (devise.en.yml, doorkeeper.de.yml, mailers.en.yml, data_resource.de.yml). Database schema, migrations, and seed data are in db/; deployment concerns are in Dockerfile, docker-compose*.yml, and docker/ (nginx.conf, entrypoint.sh, database.yml); documentation in doc/ plus README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md; static content in public/; reusable code and rake tasks in lib/. Inside app/, responsibilities are cleanly divided: controllers, models, views, jobs (gtfs_importer_job.rb, waste_notification_job.rb), mailers (defect_report_mailer.rb, notification_mailer.rb), services (category_service.rb, push_notification.rb, weather_map_service.rb), channels, and a self-contained graphql/ API layer (schema, mutations, resolvers, types). Minor observations: mailer previews are placed under spec/mailers/previews/ rather than a conventional previews location; docker/unicorn.rb looks like a leftover from a previous server now replaced by config/puma.rb; and an initializer named refresh_external_reference_unique_id.rb suggests some data-related behavior may live in configuration. None of these undermines the overall strong, well-organized separation of concerns.

modularity:
Score (avg): 4.0
[QWEN] Question evaluated: "The project demonstrates good modularity with a logical breakdown of components or modules." The project shows a strong, logical modular breakdown. The GraphQL API layer is decomposed into a schema file (smart_village_app_mainserver_schema.rb), reusable base classes (base_mutation.rb, base_object.rb, base_enum.rb, base_input_object.rb, base_interface.rb, base_union.rb), and per-operation files under mutations/ (create_tour.rb, vote_for_survey.rb, import_gtfs_feeds.rb), resolvers/ (tours_search.rb, weather_search.rb, categories_search.rb), and types/ with further sub-packages input_types/ and query_types/. Models use an elegant composition pattern: reusable attribute modules in data_resources/resource_modules/ (address.rb, contact.rb, price.rb, geo_location.rb, media_content.rb, opening_hour.rb, web_url.rb, certificate.rb, region.rb) are shared by resource models in data_resources/ (attraction.rb, news_item.rb, event_record.rb, point_of_interest.rb, generic_item.rb). Domain features are grouped into namespaces — models/survey/, models/waste/, models/notification/ — and public_transportation/ appears consistently as a module across models (travel_time.rb), GraphQL types (route_type.rb, trip_type.rb), and services (import_service.rb). Cross-cutting behaviors are extracted into concerns (models/concerns/searchable.rb, sortable.rb, filter_by_role.rb; controllers/concerns/sortable_controller.rb), and business logic is isolated in single-responsibility service objects (api_request_service.rb, clean_up_service.rb, language_service.rb, recurring_dates_for_event_service.rb) and jobs. Small caveats keep this from a 5: some namespace boundaries are ambiguous — a top-level survey.rb exists alongside a survey/ directory, notification.rb alongside notification/, data_resources/tour.rb sits next to data_resources/waste/ and data_resources/waste/tour.rb, and the file waste_location_type_type.rb carries a redundant "type_type" name — which can make module boundaries slightly harder to read. Overall, the breakdown is logical, feature-oriented, and well factored.
